A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Segment then Splat. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 includes an additional appendix, which was also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments on four datasets and ablations of object supervision and partial mask filtering.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds tracking ablations, per-scene results and reconstruction-quality comparisons.

M1.justification: The tracking strategies, object-specific Gaussian initialization, losses, staged granularity optimization, partial mask filtering and CLIP querying remain unchanged. The revised filtering threshold is an experimental-setting change, not a new method component.

E1.justification: The four segmentation datasets are retained; Neu3D is the renamed Plenoptic Video dataset, with matching citations, examples and aggregate results. v2 adds explicit novel-view-synthesis comparisons across all four datasets, extending reconstruction evaluation beyond v1's PSNR ablation on selected LERF_OVS and HyperNeRF scenes.

E2.justification: Gaussian Grouping, labeled G-Grouping, joins the static segmentation comparisons in v2 Table 1(a), appendix Tables 6–7 and Figure 4. Existing comparators remain. Newly discussed 4D LangSplat and 4-LEGS are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds tracking-component evaluation using object recall and duplicate counts, a stride experiment testing 1, 4, 7 and 10 with normalized runtime, and reconstruction comparisons using PSNR, LPIPS and SSIM. Separately, the stated mask-filtering threshold changes from 70% to 30%. Original iteration budgets and stage schedules remain; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained supervision-count and mask-filtering ablations, v2 Table 2(c) isolates the three tracking components, testing recall and redundant tracking. Appendix Table 3 examines detection-stride sensitivity and its runtime tradeoff. These directly evaluate a central module previously lacking component-level validation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The new frame-averaged recall metric does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original aggregate segmentation scores and the two original ablation tables retain their numerical entries. v2 adds Gaussian Grouping results, including 29.59 and 76.24 mIoU on LERF_OVS and 3DOVS, tracking and stride results, per-scene breakdowns, reconstruction metrics and additional qualitative examples. These substantially expand the reported evidence without demonstrating an improvement over v1's retained scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds Equation (12), defining object recall rate as a frame-averaged ratio of tracked objects to ground-truth objects. The method's mathematical formulations in Equations (1)–(11) remain equivalent; no new theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The central unified static/dynamic segmentation contribution is retained. v2 strengthens the geometry claim from improved boundaries and geometry to explicitly eliminating both geometric and semantic ambiguity, particularly in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: New Section 6 identifies concrete applicability limits: tracking failures among dense, visually similar objects and inability to handle relational queries spanning multiple objects. v2 also interprets the tracking components' recall–duplication tradeoff, explains the Figurines recall drop and discusses detection-stride efficiency. These add substantial qualifications and mechanism analysis absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a single RTX A6000 GPU and revises the documented filtering threshold. The detailed training-stage schedule in Appendix 7.1 was already present in v1 Section 4.2, so its relocation is not new reproducibility information. The project access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of 4D LangSplat and 4-LEGS, cites Gaussian Grouping and SAMURAI, and refreshes navigation and grasping references while removing several editing and SLAM citations. The central positioning around segmentation before reconstruction remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and author block, rewrites contribution bullets and selected prose, consolidates experimental setup subsections, folds querying into Section 3.5 and relocates training schedules to the appendix. Most existing methodological exposition and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a single-column NeurIPS layout, relocating and resizing displays. Original result and ablation tables are consolidated into multipart tables, Figure 4 gains a comparator and revised examples, and the appendix adds Figures 7–8 and several tables.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's missing tracking-component validation and makes scene-level performance, reconstruction quality and practical limitations more transparent. However, the unexplained 70%-to-30% threshold revision and conflicting HyperNeRF training times between Tables 2(a) and 4 leave reporting incompletely reconciled. The added evidence supports a positive but limited overall quality gain.
